                    ### Question
                    Does it indicate which of the following statements in reference to factor V of Leiden is true?

                    ### Options
                    opa. It is the resistance of factor V to the action of protein S.
opb. It is an acquired disorder that is associated with the presence of anticardiolipin antibodies.
opc. Its presence causes a prolongation of the partial thromboplastin time.
opd. Together with the prothrombin mutation, it constitutes the most frequent genetic-based thrombotic predisposition in our environment.

### Enhanced Information (For Contextual Support):
Factor V Leiden is a genetic mutation that causes resistance to activated protein C, leading to increased thrombin generation and a higher risk of venous thromboembolism. It is not an acquired disorder and does not relate to anticardiolipin antibodies, making option opb false. The mutation does not prolong the partial thromboplastin time (PTT), which remains normal in affected individuals, thus option opc is also false. Factor V Leiden is one of the most common genetic risk factors for thrombosis and often occurs alongside the prothrombin G20210A mutation, together constituting a frequent genetic-based thrombotic predisposition, supporting option opd as true.
